mainEntity.name: What is a crypto YouTube influencer agency and who is it for?

acceptedAnswer.text: A crypto YouTube influencer agency sources, vets and manages long-form creator partnerships for Web3 projects, handling everything from creator selection and narrative briefing to deal negotiation and post-campaign reporting. It is best suited to protocols, tokens and dApps that benefit from a genuine 10- to 30-minute explanation, where a short Twitter shill will not convert a serious investor or developer. Shilika Jain runs this as a fractional service for $5K–$12K/month, bundled with PR when a coordinated campaign is needed.

mainEntity.name: How much do crypto YouTube influencer campaigns cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Creator rates by tier: nano channels (10K–50K subscribers) run $200–$1,500 per video; micro channels (50K–200K) run $500–$5,000; mid-tier (200K–1M) run $10,000–$30,000; macro channels (1M+) run $25,000–$100,000 or more. A managed campaign covering 5–10 vetted creators across tiers typically runs $15,000–$40,000 all in, including agency coordination.

mainEntity.name: Which YouTube creators or channels do you work with?

acceptedAnswer.text: Creator selection depends entirely on your project category and target audience. English-language crypto YouTube covers general DeFi, trading and infrastructure channels. Beyond that, Korean, Japanese, Vietnamese, Spanish and Hindi crypto YouTube communities are accessed through vetted native-language creators. No creator shortlist is offered upfront because relevance is determined by your narrative, your audience geography and your launch timing, not by a pre-baked roster.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to go live with a YouTube campaign?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard campaign takes three to five weeks from brief to first video live: one week for creator audit and shortlisting, one week for outreach and deal close, one week for script review and approval, then publication. Rush timelines of two to three weeks are possible for smaller creator counts. Embargo-coordinated campaigns, where YouTube videos publish on the same day as press coverage, require four to six weeks of lead time to align all parties.
